note: The built-in shop rules profile, each value carrying the guideline it stands for in our own words. A profile note names any value still to spot check.

profiles.name: Generic
profiles.note: A strict preliminary check: the strictest of the values laser-cutting and press-brake shops commonly publish, read on 2026-11-25. A shop adds rules of its own (materials, sizes, per-material limits), so save your shop's numbers as a preset and check against that before ordering. It has no stock list or sheet size, which differ from shop to shop. A spot check is still wanted for hole to bend, which some pages measure to the bend line and others to the bend region; the default here (to where the bend starts) is the stricter reading.

sources.says: every cut path on one designated cut layer, with construction geometry and notes on other layers or deleted: a single-layer file has no other layer, so it leaves bend lines and notes out
all cut-path geometry on the same layer; guides, construction lines and notes moved off it or deleted
each STEP file holds exactly one solid sheet-metal body; multi-body solids and assemblies are not processed in one part file
the STEP file holds a single solid sheet-metal body; files with several bodies or assemblies do not upload
for a part bent in one piece, every feature is modelled at the same sheet thickness; thicknesses are the listed stock
thickness is uniform, with a face at every edge, and modelled at the stock thickness that will be ordered
laser holes at least 0.5 times the thickness (capability table), at least 50% of the thickness in the guide
laser holes and cut-outs at least 50% of the material thickness; the exact figure per material is on each material page
cutting holes at least half the sheet thickness
cutting holes also at least 1 mm across, whatever the thickness
hole edge to sheet edge at least 1.5 times the thickness; more for heavily formed or loaded parts (blog)
a hole at least 2 times the thickness from an edge (this one material page; the guideline page gives no figure)
holes at least 2 times the thickness from the bend line as a starting point; the page adds that the hole edge to the bend region is what counts, and that tight radii or large holes call for more
hole edge to the bend tangent line at least 2 times the thickness (rules table; its mistakes table says 1.5 to 2 times)
hole to bend line at least 2 times the thickness plus the bend radius (formula in the bending section)
flange at least 3 times the thickness; varies with press brake tooling and die width
minimum flange length is 4 times the thickness, so the flange sits stably on the lower die
the tap-size pilot hole is what goes in the 2D or 3D model (a drill chart is given); the page does not say to model the thread itself
model a plain hole at the size listed for the tap; the laser-cut hole is resized to the drill size automatically
all final cut paths go on one designated cut layer; construction geometry and notes go on other layers or are deleted
all cut-path geometry on the same layer; guides and construction lines moved off it or deleted
every cut path forms a fully closed shape; duplicate, overlapping and intersecting entities are deleted
every cut path is a closed shape; no shared or overlapping lines inside a part
all text converted to vector outlines; editable text cannot be recognised as cutting geometry
text converted to outlines; text that can still be edited does not cut
